outcome: Anal sphincter integrity (assessed by endoanal ultrasound)
Occurrence of second anal sphincter tear
cohort: 557 antenatal patients with a documented obstetric anal sphincter injury at a previous delivery
finding: The majority of women with a history of anal sphincter injury had minimal or no faecal incontinence symptoms and experienced no significant change in continence following either vaginal or caesarean delivery.
mod_finding: 70% of women with a history of anal sphincter injury went on to have a vaginal delivery, with little impact on faecal continence.
